newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil CNI president calls for approval of reforms.
newsitem.headline: Brazil CNI president calls for approval of reforms.

text.p: The president of Brazil's private National Industry Confederation (CNI) said congressional approval of a number of structural reforms was crucial to the stability and growth of the economy.
The Brazilian Congress has been slow to pass into law the government's tax, civil service and pension reforms designed to rein in the public sector deficit.
"Without the reforms, the risk to the stability of the economy is increased which in turn undermines economic growth," said Fernando Bezerra, according to a CNI statement.
"We are against delaying the reforms yet again until 1999. A period of two years might be normal in national politics, but in the world of competition it is an eternity," he added.

Bezerra said in order to create the number of jobs needed, Brazil had to invest 25 percent of gross domestic product and grow at least six percent a year, as opposed to current investment of 16 percent of GDP and economic growth of three percent.
"This is insufficient and it opens up ample opportunities for social tension," he said.

Like the Real anti-inflation plan, introduced almost three years ago, more jobs and better income distribution would bring more of Brazil's 160 million potential consumers into the market and stimulate economic growth, Bezerra said.
((-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
